items.title: 2 S&P 500 stocks to consider right now and 1 we find risky
items.summary: The S&P 500 (^GSPC) is home to the biggest and most well-known companies in the market, making it a go-to index for investors seeking stability. But not all large-cap stocks are created equal - some are struggling with slowing growth, declining margins, or increased competition.

items.title: 3 Stocks for Higher Cash Yields as Rates Stay Elevated
items.summary: When interest rates climb quickly and government debt sits at record levels, cash suddenly feels powerful again. Short-duration cash and ultra-low-risk fixed-income vehicles can become a rare source of comfort when funding costs rise and AI-related borrowing heads toward an estimated US$600b by 2026. This article pinpoints 3 stocks tied to that story and explains how each one could help you rethink where your short-term money works hardest. The three examples below are only a starting sample...

items.title: State Street Rolls Out 401(k)-Friendly Share Class of SPYM
items.summary: The company, which has ambitions to expand the reach of its ETF strategies into defined contribution plans, is among the first to add a mutual-fund share class of an ETF.

items.title: Diversified Growth or Regional Yield? How to Evaluate KBE and IAT
items.summary: KBE delivered $1,328 on a $1,000 five-year investment versus IAT's $1,057, but IAT's 2.7% dividend yield tops KBE's 2.2%. Risk tolerance and income needs will determine your pick.

items.title: 1 cash-heavy stock worth your attention and 2 we avoid
items.summary: A cash-heavy balance sheet is often a sign of strength, but not always. Some companies avoid debt because they have weak business models, limited expansion opportunities, or inconsistent cash flow.

items.title: BNY Holds $63 Trillion for Clients and Will Now Custody XRP. What If 0.1% of That Went Into XRP?
items.summary: BNY now custodies XRP for a bank holding $63 trillion in client assets, and XRP holders are already doing the math on what even a sliver of that figure could mean for the price. The case for optimism has a problem hiding in plain sight.

items.title: How Wall Street’s $30 Trillion Tokenization Push Will Reshape Investing
items.summary: Firms with agreements to use the new service include Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, Morgan Stanley and State Street.

items.title: Which Real Estate ETF Is the Better Buy: State Street’s XLRE or Northern Trust’s Global GQRE?
items.summary: XLRE holds 30 S&P 500 real estate stocks with a 0.08% expense ratio, while GQRE spreads across 201 global holdings and yields 4.4% annually.
